evals.prompt: I have a 74-minute founder interview at recordings/founder-interview.mp4 and an automatic VTT at transcripts/founder-interview.vtt. Develop a 4-minute podcast storyline collaboratively. The guest's most interesting material may be the claim that automation made apprentices more valuable rather than replacing them. Keep the host meaningfully present, but do not pad the cut just to equalize airtime. Nothing tied to the guest's former employer may appear—not its name, products, clients, team details, or anecdotes that would identify it. Give me three genuinely different arcs with complete reading-order scripts and your recommendation, then wait for my feedback and explicit approval before any editor handoff.
evals.expected_output: Creates editorial-options.md, not approved-script.md: a complete source inventory and timing-quality note; global privacy/legal constraint; transcript-grounded theme and non-obvious-claim analysis; three thesis-level distinct arcs with full verbatim reading-order scripts, functional host turns, clearly labeled editorial cards/narration, rough estimated source windows, honest runtime ranges, risks, comparison, recommendation, and pending-approval state.
expectations: The three options differ in premise, central tension, claim hierarchy, and ending rather than only clip order or titles.
All speaker text is treated as recorded verbatim material and every non-spoken line is explicitly labeled.
Former-employer exclusions are applied to indirect identifiers across all options and notes.
The response does not create approved-script.md or begin media editing without explicit approval.

evals.prompt: Turn the 58-minute product-leadership webinar in media/webinar.mov plus media/webinar-transcript.json into options for a 2:30 highlight. There is a moderator and three panelists; do not force every speaker into every option, but preserve any moderator question needed to make an answer honest. No new narration, and title cards must be restrained and explicitly editorial. Please research the guests' current public roles only if it materially helps judge which claims would surprise this audience. I want three complete arcs, including one that centers a disagreement about whether metrics improve craft, and I want a decision log that will survive several rounds of feedback.
evals.expected_output: Creates editorial-options.md with an inventory of media/transcript timing quality, optional-research decision and citations if used, claim ledger, three substantively different full scripts, transparent speaker omissions, function-based moderator presence, no narration, labeled cards, runtime accounting, constraint pass, recommendation, and a durable decision log awaiting explicit approval.
expectations: Research remains separate from recorded dialogue and is skipped or sourced with a stated editorial purpose.
Moderator and panelist selection is justified by narrative function rather than equal airtime.
The disagreement arc preserves qualifications and source context instead of overstating conflict.
Runtime estimates include spoken words, cards, pauses, and transitions and are presented as ranges.

evals.prompt: We have finished revising editorial-options.md against the meeting recording and timestamped transcript. I explicitly approve Arc 2, revision 4, exactly as written. Produce the approved editorial handoff for the video editor. Keep the target at 3:00–3:20, preserve the exclusion register and rejected-ending decision, and make it impossible for the editor to mistake the rough transcript windows for exact cut points. Do not make the video or improve any dialogue while transferring the script.
evals.expected_output: Creates a complete approved-script.md matching Arc 2 revision 4 and does not edit media. The handoff includes source inventory, locked constraints, target runtime, premise, ordered verbatim speaker turns with rough source windows, any explicitly labeled editorial items, omissions, visual notes, runtime accounting, exact approval record, integrity checks, and a clear instruction to align complete sentence boundaries against timestamped audio.
expectations: Approval status names Arc 2 revision 4 and records the explicit approval evidence.
No new or polished dialogue, cards, ending, or other material editorial change appears in the handoff.
Every rough source window is described as an editorial estimate or search neighborhood, never a frame-accurate cut point.
The handoff tells the editor to return source mismatches for editorial review rather than substitute nearby wording.

evals.prompt: We approved approved-script.md for a 75-second interview cut. The source is media/remote-call.mp4, a side-by-side recording, and the handoff has rough windows for six exact speaker turns plus a legal exclusion covering all employer-specific claims. Build a portable edit-plan.json, recover the real sentence boundaries from the media rather than estimating from transcript position, configure full-frame host/guest crops from the probed dimensions, render a restrained title and outro with the approved clips, and verify the final H.264/AAC MP4 end to end. Do not use fake AI interface graphics or invent connective dialogue.
evals.expected_output: An approved-script-gated production workflow that probes media, source-verifies and aligns all six complete verbatim turns, excludes employer-specific material everywhere, writes a strict portable edit-plan.json, renders with the bundled helper, and reports ffprobe, full-decode, visual, silence, black-frame, and human-review evidence.

evals.prompt: Before we spend time rendering, audit production/edit-plan.json against recordings/interview.mov. I suspect one guest crop extends past the source width, two clips reuse overlapping audio, an outro card is mislabeled as verbatim, and a cut ends after the file duration. Use the podcast video renderer's validation path and explain the concrete plan corrections. Do not invoke FFmpeg until the plan is valid, and do not change approved-script.md.
evals.expected_output: The helper rejects the malformed plan before FFmpeg rendering, identifies strict field/provenance, crop-bound, overlap, and duration failures, and proposes plan-only corrections that retain the approved phrases and approval boundary.

evals.prompt: Make the approved short-podcast video from two camera files listed in approved-script.md; each file has its corresponding recorded audio. The rough timestamps were generated from transcript positions and are clearly wrong, so re-transcribe the independent candidate windows with word timestamps in parallel, merge them in approved reading order, and keep each phrase complete. Use plan-relative paths, named crops for each source, 1280x720 at 30 fps, stereo loudness normalization, simple editorial title/outro cards without assuming a font installed at a fixed path, then render and produce the exact smoke-check artifacts I should inspect.
evals.expected_output: A parallel but race-free timestamp-recovery process, exact recorded-phrase alignment, a multi-source portable edit-plan.json with configurable crops/audio/canvas/cards, deterministic H.264/AAC rendering, and explicit metadata/decode/contact-sheet/still/silence/black-frame verification outputs.
